Routine follow-up visit for pediatric/adolescent female patient.

Chief concern: Routine health maintenance visit; no acute concerns reported.

History: Patient presents with parent/guardian for a general check-up. No active medications on file. No recent fever, cough, breathing difficulty, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, pain, or other new symptoms reported. Appetite, sleep, and activity are described as usual.

Review of systems: Negative for acute constitutional, respiratory, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, neurologic, and skin concerns.

Vital signs and growth parameters: Reviewed and documented in the chart; appropriate for age. 

Physical examination: Patient is alert, well appearing, and in no acute distress. Head and neck examination is normal. Tympanic membranes and oropharynx are unremarkable. Heart has regular rate and rhythm without murmur. Lungs are clear to auscultation with normal respiratory effort. Abdomen is soft and nontender without palpable masses. Skin is warm and intact without concerning lesions. Neurologic examination is age appropriate and nonfocal.

Assessment: Routine pediatric health examination without abnormal findings.

Plan: Continue age-appropriate nutrition, regular physical activity, adequate sleep, dental hygiene, and use of appropriate safety measures. Review immunization record and update as indicated. Discuss preventive care and age-appropriate anticipatory guidance with patient and parent/guardian. Return for the next routine health visit or sooner for new or worsening concerns.
